$comment: Rule catalog — error handling and observability. Standard 48. Logging secrets routes to security.no-secrets-in-artifacts (Standard 16 R2); duplicate-on-retry routes to Standard 13.

rules.title: Exceptions are not silently swallowed
rules.description: No catch block is empty of both handling code and a justification comment. Rethrowing, logging, returning a structured error, and translating to a domain error are all handling.
rules.rationale: The source prohibits an empty catch without explicit justification, so the comment at the catch site is what turns a swallowed failure into a considered one.
rules.remediation: Handle the exception, rethrow it, or state at the catch site why nothing downstream depends on it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Partial: a catch that logs at debug level and continues is shaped like handling and behaves like swallowing, and structure cannot distinguish them.

rules.title: Failure is not reported as success
rules.description: No operation that failed reports success, at any boundary — including returning successful HTTP status semantics for a failed request. Partial success is a distinct, representable state and is not this rule's subject.
rules.rationale: There is no supported reason to tell a caller that something happened when it did not, which is why no exception exists.
rules.remediation: Return the structured error the failure produced, or the partial-success shape Standard 14 R5 provides.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a returned success is truthful requires knowing what the operation was supposed to do, which no scan has.

rules.title: Retries are bounded
rules.description: No retry loop runs without a bound. A supervised long-lived connection may reconnect indefinitely where it uses bounded backoff and reports the reconnecting state.
rules.rationale: An unbounded retry converts a failure into a hang, and holds the failing dependency under load precisely when it is least able to bear it.
rules.remediation: Add an attempt or time bound with backoff, and surface the exhausted state as a structured error.
rules.$assuranceNote: A retry ceiling is often expressed in configuration rather than code, so a source scan would report on only some of the projects it examined.

rules.title: Failure paths remain observable
rules.description: No telemetry is removed solely to suppress errors or noise, and no operation is described as observable while its critical failure paths emit nothing.
rules.rationale: Reducing log volume is legitimate work; the tell is that the signal survives while the volume drops. Removing the signal produces a system whose dashboards are clean because the failures no longer reach them.
rules.remediation: Name the signal that now carries the failure — a metric, an alert, or a retained structured log — in the same change that removes the old one.
rules.$assuranceNote: Requires knowing which failure paths are critical for this system, which is a project fact rather than a code property.
